message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (A**hole I**n** The** A**ct**) for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, my brother and I live with our parents. He's 30 and went back to school after being in a bad job, which is why he moved back in about 11 months ago. I'm 21, in my third year of university, working to put myself through school, and studying business. I'm finding it difficult but manageable, and I should graduate in two years. When I started university, I began saving a bit from all my paycheques. Sometimes it was as much as 15%, other times as low as 1%, but I've managed to save about $2800 so far. My plan is to use this money for a big vacation after graduation, probably a cruise or a trip to Japan or Europe, places I've never been to. My brother hasn't been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. Our parents already help him financially, so he wouldn't ask them for more help for that. Last week, when he was complaining to my parents about not being able to go on a vacation, they mentioned my vacation fund and suggested that he could have been doing something similar all these years to afford a trip, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. Three days ago, my brother came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or fall. He said since I won't need it for another two years, there's plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. Now, my brother is really mad at me. He says it's not fair because, as the youngest child, I get to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He also says it's not fair that I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went, whereas he had to go back. He even says I've only been able to save so much money because mom and dad spoiled me. I disagree with him. My father, as well as my university accounting and finance classes, taught me to budget. If anything, I think my parents spoiled him because he doesn't know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don't think it's fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I'm also uncomfortable because I doubt he'll be able to pay me back in time, even if he could. So, am I being AITA for refusing to loan him my vacation money? Let's break this down. First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA is when someone is being unnecessarily harsh or unreasonable in a situation, often involving money or personal space. It's about whether the person's actions are justified or not. In this case, I'm refusing to lend my brother money that I've saved up for my future vacation. He's asking to borrow it so he can go on a trip to Japan this summer or fall. He argues that since I won't need the money for another two years, he has plenty of time to pay me back. However, I'm concerned about his ability to repay the loan, given his history of being bad with money. He also brings up fairness issues, saying it's not fair that I get to go on a vacation while he doesn't, especially since he had to move back in with our parents after trying to get out of a bad job by going back to school. He feels that I've been spoiled by our parents, which has allowed me to save up this money, while he hasn't had the same opportunities. I, on the other hand, feel that I've been responsible with my money, budgeting and saving consistently, which has allowed me to build up this fund. I don't think it's fair for me to give up my vacation money, especially since I'm not confident he'll be able to pay me back in time. So, is my refusal to lend him the money justified, or am I being AITA?
